hook.text: TCP/IP is the language every internet device speaks. Two protocols, invented in 1974, that connect 5 billion people.

buildup.text: IP handles addressing: every device gets a unique number. TCP handles reliability: lost packets get resent.

discovery.text: TCP adds error detection, ordering, and flow control. It turns an unreliable network into a reliable channel.

twist.text: IP is deliberately unreliable. It just delivers packets—no guarantees. Reliability is built on top, not baked in.

climax.text: This layered design lets the internet evolve. New applications run on TCP/IP without changing the network itself.

punchline.text: IP delivers. TCP ensures. Together they are the internet.

quiz.question: What does TCP add on top of IP?
options: Reliability through error detection and retransmission
